title: Rabbi Eliezer ben Dehavai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A precious saying of his remains to us in [Tractate Kallah Rabbati, end of chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Kallah_Rabbati.2.15): “Whoever greets his teacher [as an equal], whoever says something he did not hear from his teacher, and whoever sets up a rival academy against his teacher causes the Divine Presence to depart from Israel; and whoever says something in his teacher’s name brings redemption to the world.” This statement is cited in [Berakhot 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.27b.2), where the words “ben Dehavai” are missing.

notes.text: החולק על ישיבתו is rendered setting up a rival academy against one’s teacher, rather than merely debating the academy. Saved Davidson Berakhot 27b confirms the warning and lacks ben Dehavai as Hyman reports. The [as an equal] greeting gloss remains editorial.

The linked Kallah Rabbati text names Rabbi Eliezer ben Dehavai and continues with the statement about repeating a teaching in one’s teacher’s name. The linked Bavli names Rabbi Eliezer without the patronymic and gives the warning, with a further clause about praying behind one’s teacher. Hyman gives an abbreviated quotation.
